input: A floor for choosing which new transients receive a spectrum is priced from a paper's architecture comparison: a metadata-only network reaches 91.2% policy purity against 93.0% for a multimodal image-plus-metadata network, 98% of the ceiling, both on the paper's test split. The paper trains 20 trials of the multimodal network with identical hyperparameters and states that the trial with the best test-split performance is chosen as the production model, whose numbers the table reports. How the metadata-only network's reported model was chosen is not stated. Price the floor share.

SYNTHETIC. The decision to be benchmarked is the automatic classification report issued for a spectrum that has already been taken. A template-matching floor and a recurrent-network ceiling are each run once on the same 1,011 held-out spectra, both scored as true-positive rate at under 1% false-positive rate. The recurrent network's architecture, epoch and score cut were chosen on a disjoint 1,016-spectrum set, and the template tool's match threshold was fixed before the held-out set was opened. Placeholder values: floor 0.55, ceiling 0.83. Price the floor share.

A floor for choosing which new transients receive a spectrum at first alert uses only Galactic latitude, computed from the alert position at first detection. Two learners were declared before the run and both are reported: gradient boosting AUC 0.537, logistic regression AUC 0.510, grouped 5-fold cross-validation over 7,843 classified objects with groups merging positions within 3 arcsec; a label-permutation control gave 0.486. The 3,374 unclassified objects are excluded and the exclusion is disclosed. No ceiling has been measured on first-alert inputs. State the floor.
